patients.summary: Graphic designer who joined in 2018 with recurrent mouth ulcers, then developed iron deficiency, SLE, celiac disease with dermatitis herpetiformis, and later cold then warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia managed by outside hematology. Last seen December 2025 while tapering prednisone.

events.reason: New patient, establish care and yearly exam

conditions.label: Recurrent aphthous stomatitis
conditions.note: A few episodes a year since her teens; OTC gels

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26 yo woman new to the practice, moving her care closer to home in Easthampton. Works as a graphic designer, mostly at a desk, some freelance at night.

PMH: mouth ulcers since roughly high school, a few flares a year, small and sore, last about a week, she uses an OTC numbing gel. Never needed anything stronger. Otherwise healthy.
PSH: none.
Meds: none.
Allergies: none known to medications.
FHx: mother has lupus. Maternal grandmother had rheumatoid arthritis. Paternal aunt with celiac. Father has type 2 diabetes.
Social: never smoked. A drink or two a month. Lives alone, rents. Walks and does some yoga.
Gyn: regular cycles. Last Pap last year at her old office, she says normal; records requested.

ROS negative today, no current mouth sores.

Exam: well, pleasant. Vitals as charted. Oropharynx clear, no ulcers. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Skin without rash. Joints full range, no synovitis.

A/P
1. Preventive care: Tdap today (no record of one as an adult). CBC, CMP, TSH. Offered one-time HIV and hep C screening, she accepts. PHQ-2 0.
2. Recurrent aphthous ulcers: mild and infrequent. Keep using the gel; let me know if she has one that lasts beyond two weeks.
Follow up yearly, flu shot in the fall.

documents.title: Vaccine Administration
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Tdap 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS given. Tolerated well, waited 10 minutes, no reaction.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Zoe, all of your bloodwork came back normal: blood count, kidney and liver numbers, thyroid, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nice to meet you this week. See you in the fall for a flu shot.

documents.title: Prior Primary Care Records
documents.author: outside primary care
documents.body:
Records from former primary care office, covering 2012 to 2017, received by fax.

Annual exams 2014, 2016 and 2017 without significant findings. Cervical cytology 2017: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. Prior cytology 2014 also negative. Childhood immunizations documented complete; HPV series completed in adolescence per the immunization registry print-out.
Problem list: oral aphthous ulcers, recurrent. No medications listed. Allergies: NKDA.
No hospitalizations.

Filed to chart; PCP reviewed, nothing new to act on.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for seasonal flu shot. Feels well, no fever, no egg or vaccine reactions in the past. Quadrivalent flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Tolerated without issue.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27F yearly exam. Busy spring at work, sleeping okay. Mouth ulcers about the same, two this past winter, each gone in about a week with the gel. No other concerns.

Meds: none. NKDA.
Social unchanged, nonsmoker, rare alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted, weight steady. Oral mucosa without ulcers today. Thyroid normal size. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen benign. Skin clear.

Plan: no labs needed this year, last year's all normal. Pap due 2020 by her prior schedule. PHQ-2 0. Flu shot in October. Return in a year.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Influenza Vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Seasonal flu vaccine given, left deltoid, 0.5 mL IM. No acute illness today. Left after observation, no problems.

documents.title: Visit Rescheduled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called patient about her spring physical. Office limiting routine visits for now. She is well, no concerns, agreeable to pushing her physical to the fall. Will call her back in August to book.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
28F, physical pushed from spring. Working from home since March, says she is a bit more tired than usual but blames the screen hours. Periods regular, a few days heavier. Mouth ulcers: one in the summer.

Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker.

Exam: vitals as charted. Conjunctivae maybe a touch pale. Mouth clear. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No rash. No joint swelling.

A/P
- Fatigue, mild: CBC and BMP today; if the count is low, will add iron studies onto the same tube.
- Pap: she prefers to wait until her 30s for cotesting rather than doing cytology now; last normal 2017. Reasonable, will revisit.
- Flu vaccine today. PHQ-2 1, not concerning.
Call with results.

documents.title: Vaccine Administration
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. Mask on, observed 15 min, no reaction.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times daily

documents.title: Lab Results - Iron Deficiency
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called Zoe. Hgb 10.8 with MCV 76; iron 34, TIBC 440, ferritin 8. Iron deficiency anemia, most likely from menstrual losses given her heavier days. Starting ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times a day; take with water or orange juice, not with coffee or tea; expect dark stools, some constipation is common. Recheck CBC and ferritin in 3 months. She will call if the stomach upset is too much. Sent to her pharmacy.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic request from pharmacy: ferrous sulfate 325 mg, #90. Refilled per protocol, 2 refills. Reminder sent to book lab recheck in January.
